title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 1st District
area: Western Kentucky, including Paducah, Bowling Green's western suburbs, and the Jackson Purchase and Pennyrile regions.

candidates.name: James Comer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 88.1% of the vote, defeating David Sims, Robert James Sutherby and Penny Arcos.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Kentucky's 1st District (since 2016); Chair, House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

summary.text: James Comer is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a 2016 special election. He chairs the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and previously served as Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture and in the Kentucky House of Representatives.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture from Western Kentucky University in 1993.
Served in the Kentucky House of Representatives, District 53, from 2001 to 2012, and as Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture from 2012 to 2016.
Co-owner of the Comer Land and Cattle Company since 1994; previously president of Comer and Polston Insurance Incorporated and CFB Foods Incorporated.

priorities.text: Government Oversight and Reform: says the Oversight Committee under his leadership has investigated waste, fraud, abuse and mismanagement across the federal government, including pandemic relief fraud and improper payments.
Healthcare: says he supports protecting rural healthcare providers, strengthening Medicare, and giving patients greater control over their healthcare decisions.
Second Amendment: says he is a "strong defender of the Second Amendment" who opposes federal efforts to restrict the constitutional rights of law-abiding gun owners.

positions.summary: Says he opposes federal efforts to restrict gun rights, has voted against legislation criminalizing private firearm transfers and creating a national gun registry, and supports concealed-carry reciprocity.
positions.quote: Congressman Comer is a strong defender of the Second Amendment and opposes all efforts by the federal government to restrict the constitutional rights of law-abiding citizens. He has voted against legislation that would criminalize private firearm transfers, create unnecessary delays for lawful purchases, and move the country closer to a national gun registry.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (119th Congress, 2025-2026) and also serves on the Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Chaired the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) as well.

candidates.name: Drew Williams
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary after the primary was canceled with no other candidates on the ballot.

summary.text: Drew Williams is a lifelong resident of Marshall County, Kentucky, running as the Democratic nominee. He says he wants to bring more public engagement, such as town halls and issue-driven debates, into how he would represent the district.

background.text: Graduated from Murray State University in 2016 with a degree in History with a minor in Biology.

priorities.text: "I want to formalize our public townhalls, issue-driven debates, courthouse surveys, and expert roundtables to get a true understanding and perspective of where our community stands. It is my duty to vote based on that collectively gathered soft-data while working to be an advocate for the poor, marginalized, and disenfranchised."

researchNotes: Comer's federal key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script. His official issues pages (agriculture, education, healthcare, military, small business, transportation) largely describe general priorities rather than taking a stance on one of this guide's fixed issue statements; only his Second Amendment page directly addresses one. No specific issue positions with direct quotes were found for Williams beyond his general priorities statement (from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, reproduced on the district election page).
